reviews.comment: Course was MEEN 608-Continuum Mechanics (only 305 was available to select). He's great with concepts and driving home the fundamentals. Can be pedantic if you aren't into the math and philosophy behind things. Frequent tangents. But I learned a ton and enjoyed it a lot

Unfortunately Dr. Raj had to teach through Zoom due to health issues which exacerbated the trouble many students had. His lectures were hard to follow. Though his quiz and exam problems were pulled from the book, some had unfamiliar material. While he did curve, I felt unmotivated by his delivery of the course to actively learn the material.

This seemingly 90 year old man is so dissatisfied by his life that he projects it onto his students. Awful grader, awful handwriting, doesn't teach in person, awful accent, awful grade composition, on numerous occasions he shouted "JESUS CHRIST" at a question. What a horrible person, wouldn't wish my worst enemy to have him.

Dr. Rajagopal is hands down the worst professor I have ever taken. He is extremely rude, condescending, and difficult to approach. I have never been afraid to ask a professor a question, until I took his class. He over complicates simple concepts, and his lectures are almost entirely useless. Watch Jeff Hanson if you want a chance of passing.

Dr. Raj is the worst professor I have had in college thus far. He is rude to his students when they ask questions, cannot attend class in person due to health issues, and teaches the class at a graduate level that makes it very confusing to follow during his lectures. Avoid taking undergraduate classes with him at all cost.

Texas A&M University should be paying me to take this course from Rajagopal. There was a large disconnect between Rajagopal and his students which made this course very painful. In our six week of classes we were still on the second week of information. All of this because he would rather disprove the textbook than teach the course.
